To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of aFGF and either IBMX or forskolin can induce the expression of tyrosine-hydroxylase in cultured neurons of the striatal region of rat brain, and that the combination of all four molecules can result in maximal expression of TH in striatal neurons.
the synergistic combination of aFGF and co-activators, including activators of the PKA pathway, can novelly induce TH gene expression in cultured striatal neurons.
aFGF can induce expression of TH in non-TH-expressing brain neurons, and this can be potentiated by co-treatment with co-activators such as DA, TPA, PKC activators, and PKA activators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the induction of the TH gene in non-TH neurons.
identifying and characterizing the molecular mechanisms which direct TH gene expression in brain neurons.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the TH gene in neurons of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aFGF and co-activating factors, such as DA, PKC and PKA activators, synergistically induce TH expression in striatal neurons.
the synergistic combination of aFGF and co-activator agents results in a novel expression of the TH gene in non-TH-expressing neurons of the brain.
aFGF is the primary signal for the induction of the TH gene and that the co-activating agents are required for the synergistic induction of TH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are multiple signaling pathways that direct the initiation of TH gene expression in cultured neurons, each of which involves the synergy of specific co-activators and aFGF.
the induction of TH by a growth factor is not a simple process but requires a complex series of events.
there are multiple signaling pathways which converge to induce TH gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of TH in non-TH neurons is a complex process that is not dependent upon a single growth factor or signaling pathway.
the initiation of TH expression can be accomplished in multiple ways and that the combination of all co-activating signals together is required for the maximal expression of the enzyme.
there are multiple signaling pathways which can be used to induce expression of TH.
